$comment: Merging lexemes (ADR 0158) on zz, an invented fixture language given whole: a language that states `requires` per category merges lexemes; a token's values are what its lexemes bring (`realises`); merging runs outward from the base, and a lexeme merges only where its `on` holds on the word as it stands (its side, the part of speech, values it has, values it needs, the word complete); no feature is brought twice; what its category and its lexemes require and nothing brings is `missing`; a form stored for the merged word covers the lexemes whose values it has.

vectors.note: A verb merged with the perfect and its 1sg ending: every requirement met (VERB requires Aspect; the perfect requires Person and Number); its values are what its lexemes bring.
Zero morphemes (the owner: 0-morphemes can exist): the perfect and the 3sg write nothing, and still bring their values.
Finite-ness requires person and number: the perfect raises them and nothing meets them, so the word is incomplete.
A verb alone is never a word: its category requires Aspect.
The perfect's 1sg ending merges only onto a word that has Aspect=Perf.
The plural merges onto nouns only.
An ending whose entry says it stands after its base (on.at) is not merged before it.
An enclitic onto a complete word (on.complete): after the person ending.
The same enclitic merged before the person ending: the word is not yet complete.
A suffix that needs some value for Person (on.needs), after the ending that brings it.
The same suffix merged before it: no Person yet.
A noun requires Number; the singular is a zero morpheme.
A form stored for the merged word (an irregular plural) stands for the lexemes whose values it covers: the plural's -a is in it, not joined to it.
